description:
Freeze the before figure for `crates/jit/src` production lines, counted the way the epic's Background describes, so the completion report states a reproducible delta.

## Background

The epic's survey counts production lines excluding `#[cfg(test)]` blocks, test-only sibling modules, doc comments and blank lines. The planning investigation's counter, `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/prodlines.py`, implements exactly that in its default mode, reporting per top-level module; at 21f9e563 it yields 66,372. The survey's stated figure of about 63,100 is reproduced only with `--strip-line-comments --test-support-as-test` (63,118), which also drops plain comments and `test-support`-gated code. The figure moves with every commit of this and concurrent epics, so the baseline must be pinned to a named commit taken before this epic first changes `crates/jit/src`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The counter is committed as `scripts/production-lines.py` with unchanged definitions and flags, so the reports and the budget script share one implementation; the planning copy stays as investigation evidence.
- [hard] REQ-02: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/line-count-baseline.md` records per-module and total production lines in the default (survey-described) mode as the authoritative figures, with the flagged-mode figures beside them.
- [hard] REQ-03: The document names the full commit SHA measured and the exact commands, and that commit precedes every commit of this epic that changes `crates/jit/src`.
- [hard] REQ-04: Re-running the recorded commands at the recorded commit reproduces every figure.

## Notes

842b0ac6 deletes code concurrently, which is why the commit is pinned. Design rationale: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/plan.md`.
title: Record the production-line baseline for crates/jit/src
